author: United States Bureau of Yards and Docks
title: Building the Navy's Bases in World War II: History of the Bureau of Yards and Docks and the Civil Engineer Corps, 1940–1946
publisher: United States Government Printing Office, Washington
notes: The Navy's construction history, and the only work in this registry that describes the thing the Pearl Harbor counterfactual turns on: the fuel storage at Pearl Harbor and what state it was in. Cited here for a negative finding rather than a positive one. Its chapter 22 lists 'two fuel-oil tank farms (above ground)' in the pre-war navy yard and gives no capacity for them, and the six-million-barrel figure it does give belongs to the *underground* project, which was begun late in December 1940 and whose first vault was not usable until September 1942 — so that number is not a December 1941 number, however often it is quoted as one. Title, publisher, city and year read off the title page reproduced in the transcription. Same reachability note as source:morton-1962.
